verdicts.note: Cached roll calls confirm Doglio voted Yea on ESSB 6346 House final passage (2026-03-09, 51-46), ESSB 5813 (53-45) and ESHB 2081 (50-48). GetLegislation confirms she is prime sponsor of HB 1785. The ESSB 6346 vote is not her only taxes evidence, so +2 high stands under the 2026-10-08 addendum.

Rests on her EHB 1217 vote (cached: Yea on conference-report final passage, 54-44) plus her housing-funding statement and the Housing Alliance endorsement. One record vote on rent stabilization, a pole_b marker, and no supply-side language. Medium is right.
Cached roll calls confirm Yea on 2SHB 2105 (both House final-passage votes) and SSB 5855. A law-enforcement masking limit is a named pole_b marker. Two record votes support high.

Direction and magnitude hold, but nothing here is a legislative record on gender, LGBTQ+ or reproductive policy. The evidence is a past job as Pro-Choice Washington political director [S1], endorsements from Planned Parenthood Alliance, the LGBTQ+ Victory Fund and Stonewall Dems [S1][S3], and one listing on the No-on-I-638 endorser page [S16]. That is a strong endorsement pattern plus one stated stance, which the guide calls medium. Compare Parshley in LD 22 Pos 2: her high rests on a sponsored bill, HB 2657.

Cached roll calls confirm Yea on ESHB 1296 third reading (56-37) and on final passage as amended by the Senate (59-39), and Nay on the Republican floor amendments. Together with her No-on-I-1 listing [S16, cached and confirmed], that is consistent pole_b record evidence. This is parents-and-schools evidence only and does not mix in social evidence.

The basis says HB 2515 'regulates' data centers, but the dossier never describes what the bill does. It says only that she is prime sponsor of a bill 'on' or 'addressing' emerging large energy use facilities [S12] and that it passed the House 51-41 [S13]. The cached GetLegislation record has only that title. Placing her toward the 'data-center limits' pole infers from the bill's subject, not from its content or any statement she made. Keep the direction at low until the dossier records what the bill requires.

Pamphlet (page 35, checked) twice frames him as an outsider ('Don is not a professional politician. I am a regular hardworking citizen just like you') and lists no elected experience. He campaigns on non-politician status against an eight-year incumbent, so +2 high fits. That separates him from first-time candidates who were cut to medium because they did not run on renewal.
